description: Game-agnostic story formats for gameplay long-form. Templates use {slot} placeholders; plan_story_edit fills start_value, end_value, n, cold_open_label and cold_open_value from beats and takes the rest from its slots argument.

slots.game: Game name as viewers search it.
slots.role: What the player is (solo sniper, medic, builder, trader).
slots.item: The unlock, weapon, vehicle or kit at the centre of the video.
slots.build: The structure or setup being built.
slots.constraint: The rule that makes it a challenge (no vehicles, only found gear, one life).
slots.goal: The goal in a few words.
slots.open_loop: A tease of something that goes wrong or surprises later.
slots.enemy_group: The antagonist (a named squad, a full server, a 30-player clan).
slots.expensive_price: Price of the most expensive tier.
slots.metric: What a measured test measures, with units.
slots.start_value: Auto: value of the first beat that has one.
slots.end_value: Auto: value of the last beat that has one.
slots.cold_open_label: Auto: label of the cold-open beat.
slots.cold_open_value: Auto: value of the cold-open beat.

shared_recipe: Goal, plan and a 2-3 s flash-forward of the payoff inside the first 15 s.
A trackable spine (methods, price tiers, levels, episodes) with one chapter per step.
Past-tense narration bridges with open loops between steps.
Every section ends on a number the viewer can track.
A fast ending: verdict, then the subscribe ask.
The game HUD is the counter; a facecam is optional.
Thumbnail: start state vs end state with one or two huge numbers.

pacing_gate.measure: Whisper word timestamps (large-v3 recommended for comparable numbers). A dead stretch is a gap of dead_threshold_s or more with no transcribed word, including the lead-in and the tail.

formats.name: Timed money run
formats.when_to_use: A fresh economy (launch, wipe, new character) or any game with a visible money or score counter. The video answers one question: how much can this method make in a fixed time?
title_templates: How Much Money Can a {role} Make in {hours} Hours? ({game})
{start_value} to {end_value} in {hours} Hours as a {role} | {game}
I Played {game} for {hours} Hours, {constraint}. Here's What I Made

thumbnail_template.layout: Split frame: start state on the left, end state on the right, one huge number per side.
notes: Use real gameplay frames; the HUD counter is the proof.
Two numbers at most; nothing else to read.

hook_0_15s.template: 2-3 s of the final counter: {cold_open_value}.
I gave myself {hours} hours to make as much as I could in {game}, starting from {start_value}.
The plan: {plan}. {open_loop}

spine.description: One section per hour or per method, in order. Show the running total at every boundary.

formats.section_end_rule: End every section on the running total (HUD or a one-line card) before the cut.

narration.style: Past-tense VO bridges over gameplay ('By hour three I'd found...'), each ending on an open loop.
bridge_templates: By then I was at {value}, and the next part cost more than I expected.
That put me at {value}. It didn't last.

formats.chapters: One chapter per hour or method, titled with the number it ends on ('Hour 3: $48K'). The 0:00 chapter is the goal.

timing.notes: Fresh economies make the money question everyone's question. Testing it on camera beats being first.

formats.ending: Final total on screen, a one-line verdict on the method, then subscribe. Under 20 s.
pitfalls: Hiding the total until the end instead of showing it at every boundary.
Methods viewers cannot copy (admin help, exploits).
Looting or travel stretches with no narration.
A title number that first appears after minute 5.

formats.name: Unlock grind
formats.when_to_use: A new or reset progression tree where one unlock is the first-week question: how long until I get it?
title_templates: I Played {role} Until I Unlocked the {item} in {game}
How Long Does It Take a Solo {role} to Unlock the {item}? ({game})
{game}, But I Can't Stop Until I Unlock the {item}...

thumbnail_template.layout: Split frame: starter gear on the left, the unlocked item on the right; a tier or level marker on each side.
notes: The unlock screen or the item in hand is the right half.
Show the tier number or progress bar, not a paragraph.

hook_0_15s.template: 2-3 s of the unlock screen or the {item} firing.
I wasn't allowed to stop playing until I unlocked the {item}.
{n} tiers stood in the way. {open_loop}

spine.description: One section per tier, with the level or XP and the elapsed time at each boundary. Close with 30-60 s of the unlock in use.
steps: Unlock tested in a real match

formats.section_end_rule: End each tier on the level or XP number and the time spent so far.

narration.style: Past-tense VO bridges; each tier ends on an open loop about the next tier's problem.
bridge_templates: {value}, and the next tier took longer than the last two combined.
That was {value}. The next tier is where it got ugly.

formats.chapters: One chapter per tier ('Tier 2: 3h 10m'), then 'Testing the {item}'.

timing.notes: The answer goes stale once most players have the unlock.

formats.ending: The final time and level, a verdict on whether the unlock was worth it, then subscribe.
pitfalls: Skipping tiers without saying so.
Grind footage with no visible counter.
Ending on the unlock screen without showing the item work.

formats.name: Price ladder (cheap vs expensive)
formats.when_to_use: Gear with clear price tiers, especially after an economy change or in a mode that caps gear. Viewers want to know whether the expensive option is worth it.
title_templates: {cheap_price} vs {expensive_price} {item} in {game}: Is It Worth It?
Cheapest vs Most Expensive {item} ({game})
I Tested Every {item} Tier From {cheap_price} to {expensive_price}

thumbnail_template.layout: Two kits side by side, each with its total price in a big box.
notes: Same pose and background for both kits so the price is the only difference.

hook_0_15s.template: 2-3 s of the surprising result: the cheap kit winning or the expensive one failing.
Is the {expensive_price} {item} actually better than the {cheap_price} one?
{n} tiers, the same test for each. {open_loop}

spine.description: Cheapest to most expensive, every tier through the same test, with price and score on screen.

formats.section_end_rule: End each tier on its score for the same test (kills, money, time survived) next to its price.

narration.style: Scripted comparison VO, present or past tense; restate price and score at each boundary.
bridge_templates: For {value}, that's the score to beat.
{value} bought a lot less than I thought.

formats.chapters: One chapter per tier, titled with the price ('$5K kit'), then 'Verdict'.

timing.window: within 2 weeks of an economy, vendor or mode change
timing.notes: Gear-capped modes reset which tier is worth buying.

formats.ending: A score-per-price table, the pick for most players, then subscribe.
pitfalls: Changing the test between tiers.
No price on screen when a tier is introduced.
Burying the verdict after the outro.

formats.name: Build-and-payoff blueprint
formats.when_to_use: A buildable structure or setup that viewers can copy, followed by proof that it works in a real match.
title_templates: I Built a {build} Solo. Did It Pay Off?
The {build} Nobody Is Using in {game}
Solo {build} in {game}: Built in Minutes, Paid Back {end_value}

thumbnail_template.layout: The finished build from its best angle, with one benefit line and one number.
notes: Arrow to the key part of the build.
Real screenshot of the build, ideally under attack.

hook_0_15s.template: 2-3 s of the build working: {cold_open_label}.
Today I'm building a {build} alone, using only {constraint}.
The plan: {plan}. It has to pay for itself before the match ends. {open_loop}

spine.description: Supplies, placement, structure, defence, then the build tested in a real match and the payoff counted.

formats.section_end_rule: End each stage on a number: supplies left, minutes elapsed, cost so far, then kills or money once it is live.

narration.style: Instructional VO ('you'll want to...') for build stages, switching to past-tense story VO for the live test.
bridge_templates: With the walls up at {value}, the first attack came early.

formats.chapters: One chapter per build stage, then 'Live test' and 'Payoff: {end_value}'.

timing.window: any time; strongest in the first days of a wipe when everyone rebuilds
timing.notes: Sequels work well as '2.0' versions of the same build.

formats.ending: The payoff number against the cost, a one-line verdict, a pointer to the next build, then subscribe.
pitfalls: A tutorial with no live test.
Practice-range footage only.
No running cost or payoff number.

formats.name: Narrated solo story
formats.when_to_use: A solo player against a bigger force (a clan, a full server) or a role challenge ('deadliest X'). Works for viewers who do not play the game.
title_templates: How I Became {game}'s Deadliest {role}
Solo vs {enemy_group}: {goal}
This {game} Server Didn't Know I Existed...

thumbnail_template.layout: The hidden or outnumbered player on one side with 'ME' and an arrow; the unaware enemy on the other.
notes: Real screenshot of the hide or the overwatch position works if art is not an option.

hook_0_15s.template: 2-3 s of the climax: {cold_open_label}.
Me, alone, against {enemy_group}. {goal}.
The rules: {constraint}. I had {n} goals, and I couldn't log off until they were done. {open_loop}

spine.description: An N-goal contract that unlocks tiers, or acts split by base moves and rival encounters. Show the checklist count at each act break.

formats.section_end_rule: End each act on the checklist count ('3 of 10 done') or the score so far.

narration.style: Past-tense storytelling VO ('I'd soon find out...') woven with live reactions; calm, dry, amused.
bridge_templates: That made {value}. They still had no idea where I was.
{value}, and the hard part hadn't started.

formats.chapters: One chapter per act or goal, titled as a story beat ('The first ambush', 'Goal 4 of 10').

timing.window: evergreen; set it on wipe day in the story
timing.notes: Stories do not depend on the release calendar, but 'on wipe day' framing still helps.

formats.ending: The aftermath, the final count, one reflective line, then subscribe.
pitfalls: No stakes or antagonist in the first sentence.
Long silent sneaking: cut it to 4 s or less or narrate over it.
Generic AI-art thumbnails where the community dislikes them.

formats.name: Season series (rags to riches EPn)
formats.when_to_use: A launch or wipe where a broke-start series can run for weeks. The episode number becomes the reason to come back.
title_templates: How a BROKE Solo Starts... {game} (Rags to Riches EP{episode})
{goal}... {game} ({series} EP{episode})
Starting From Nothing in Season {season} of {game} (EP{episode})

thumbnail_template.layout: Series wordmark across the top, 'EP n' badge, one hero object or number.
notes: Keep the wordmark and layout identical across episodes.
The episode number must be readable at phone size.

hook_0_15s.template: 2-3 s of this episode's best moment: {cold_open_label}.
EP1: start from nothing, every session recorded, nothing off camera. Later episodes: last time I finished on {start_value}.
Today: {plan}. The craziest moment is at the end. {open_loop}

spine.description: Sessions in order, net worth or stash value at each boundary. A season reset starts a new EP1.

formats.section_end_rule: End each session on the stash or net-worth number; end the episode on the number the next one starts from.

narration.style: Hybrid: live commentary in sessions, recorded past-tense VO for the recap and between sessions.
bridge_templates: That left me at {value}. Not enough yet.
{value} in the stash, and one run I almost didn't record.

formats.chapters: One chapter per session plus 'Recap' at 0:00 and 'Where we stand' at the end.

timing.window: EP1 in the first week after a launch or wipe, then 1-2 episodes a week until mid-season
timing.notes: Missing a week breaks the habit the series depends on.

formats.ending: The closing number, what next episode is about, a comment prompt, then subscribe.
pitfalls: No episode number on the thumbnail.
Recaps longer than 20 s.
Gaps of more than a week between episodes.

formats.name: Patch-week take
formats.when_to_use: The first 24-72 h after a patch, wipe or new unlock: a fast 'X is BROKEN' first take or an N-tips list.
title_templates: {item} is BROKEN in {game}
{n} {game} Tips You Probably Didn't Know
{n} Changes in {patch} That Matter for {role}

thumbnail_template.layout: One hero image (the item, or the most surprising tip in action) with huge text built around a number or BROKEN.
notes: Tip 1 or the BROKEN claim must be what the thumbnail shows.
A circle or arrow on the one thing that matters.

hook_0_15s.template: 2-3 s of the claim in action: {cold_open_label}.
Did you know {item} can do this? I've put {hours}+ hours in, and even veterans miss it.
{n} of them, and the last one is the strangest. {open_loop}

spine.description: A numbered list; every tip or change is its own chapter and shows its effect.

formats.section_end_rule: End each tip on its measurable effect (damage, seconds saved, money, range).

narration.style: Tightly scripted VO with pauses cut out; one tip per breath.

formats.chapters: One chapter per tip, numbered ('3. Faster reloads').

timing.window: patch, wipe or unlock +0 to 48 h
timing.notes: After 72 h the take is old news.

formats.ending: The bonus tip, a comment prompt for tips that were missed, then subscribe.
pitfalls: Posting after the first 72 h.
Padding the list with weak tips.
Opinions with no numbers.

formats.name: Measured test
formats.when_to_use: A question the community argues about that can be measured: cost per kill, damage at range, time per run, percent cheaper vs percent worse.
title_templates: I Tested {item} So You Don't Have To ({metric})
Is {item} Worth It? I Measured It ({metric})
{cheap_price} Build vs {expensive_price} Build: {metric}

thumbnail_template.layout: The result number is the thumbnail; the item or chart is secondary.

hook_0_15s.template: 2-3 s of the result card: {cold_open_value}.
Everyone argues about {item}. I measured {metric}.
{n} tests, same conditions. One result surprised me. {open_loop}

spine.description: Problem, method, runs, numbers, comparison, recommendation.

formats.section_end_rule: End each test on its measured number with units and sample size.

narration.style: Tightly scripted VO; state the method once, then numbers.
bridge_templates: {value}, which is not what the patch notes suggest.

formats.chapters: Question at 0:00, one chapter per test, then 'Results' and 'Recommendation'.

timing.window: within 10 days of an update that changed the numbers
timing.notes: Make tests a recurring series so growth does not stop when the patch window closes.

formats.ending: The recommendation in one line, the next test, then subscribe.
pitfalls: One run presented as a result; always state the sample size.
Numbers without units.
A one-off test with no series behind it.
